books.section: Unit 5: Toward the Civil War and Reconstruction (1844–1877)

stimulus.source_note: Arthur Nahl, “Sutter's Mill,” painted 1851. Public domain.
stimulus.text: Arthur Nahl's 1851 painting “Sutter's Mill” shows the sawmill beside a river, with a flume carrying water to the mill, hills rising behind it, and a small settlement nearby. The mill stands at Coloma, California, on the American River, where gold was discovered in January 1848.

source: original; stimulus image from the shared pool, Arthur Nahl, “Sutter's Mill” (1851), public domain
stem: The discovery shown in the painting most directly led to which of the following?

options.text: The annexation of Texas by the United States.
options.misconception: Texas was annexed in 1845, three years before the gold discovery.

options.text: A rapid migration of hundreds of thousands to California.
The settlement of the Oregon boundary with Britain.
options.misconception: The Oregon boundary was settled by treaty in 1846, two years before the gold discovery.

options.text: The repeal of the Missouri Compromise.
options.misconception: The Missouri Compromise was repealed by the Kansas-Nebraska Act in 1854, for reasons beyond the gold rush.

rationales.A: Texas was annexed in 1845, three years before gold was found at Sutter's Mill.
rationales.B: News of the gold brought about 80,000 migrants to California in 1849 — the Forty-niners — and more than 300,000 had arrived by 1855. Background: California's population rose from about 93,000 in 1850 to about 380,000 in 1860.
rationales.C: The Oregon Treaty was signed in 1846, two years before the gold discovery.
rationales.D: The Kansas-Nebraska Act repealed the Missouri Compromise in 1854; the gold rush was not its cause.
rationales.general:
1. Name the discovery. Gold was found at Sutter's Mill in January 1848.
2. Ask what happened next. Word spread, and about 80,000 people reached California in 1849; by 1855 more than 300,000 had arrived.
3. Check the dates. Texas, Oregon, and the Missouri Compromise all belong to other years and other causes.
Remember: a discovery is a cause only when the dates line up. Gold in 1848 lines up with the rush of 1849.
